newsitem.title: UK: EU maltsters still hope for a rise in refund.
newsitem.headline: EU maltsters still hope for a rise in refund.

text.p: Maltsters are still hoping that the European Union (EU) will review its malt export refund in the coming weeks despite Thursday's decision to keep it unchanged.
"We are waiting for the (European) Commission as they said they would address the market position. We take their word that they will be doing that," said one European maltsters representative.
The EU rejected maltsters' demands for a higher subsidy and kept the refund unchanged at 32.50 Ecus per tonne for unroasted malt.

But malt exporters were awaiting a fresh consideration on the issue which has recently sparked a row with the Commission over what the malt industry says is a refund that fails to give them a level playing field in the world market.
"We have to see what happens over the next two weeks. I would have thought that sometime over that period the Commission would be addressing the issue," the malt representative said.

Maltsters said the current refund for unroasted malt is unfair when compared to export subsidies for barley. Malt subsidies are often set 30 percent above the barley refund but are currently only five percent above the latest barley subsidy.
Exporters believe very few licences will be taken out if the refund remains at the present level.

But trade sources who track EU policy reckon the Commission's refusal to raise the refund partly stemmed from the fact that the licences taken out so far already cover some 10 percent of the annual malt exports of two million tonnes.
The Commission believes that the European malt is competitive following a good barley harvest this year.
According to a monthly review system now in place the refund may not be subject to review until mid-November but maltsters say the Commission can address the issue anytime.
"If everything was just going along normally it would be normal to look once a month but the Commission can review the refund whenever they wish," said the maltsters' representative.
